sectionClause: Clause 1.1 - Defined terms / "Force Majeure Event" / paragraph (a)
clarification:

any disruption, delay or inability to transport, ship or deliver Goods arising from marine perils, acts of maritime authorities, closure or congestion of ports, shortage of vessels or containers, blockage of shipping routes, or other events affecting ocean, sea or inland waterway transportation.

Proposed amendment:
Replace:
Loss means any loss (whether direct or indirect), debt, obligation, cost (including legal costs, deductibles or increased premiums), expense, damages, fine, penalty, compensation, charge or any other liability of any kind, whether: actual, prospective or contingent; currently ascertainable or not; or arising under or for breach of contract, in tort (including negligence), restitution, or otherwise at Law.

With:

sectionClause: Clause 30.2 Limitation of Supplier’s liability / paragraph (d)
clarification:

Notwithstanding anything else contained in this Contract to the contrary, the Supplier shall not be liable under, arising out of or in connection with the Contract (to the fullest extent permitted at law) whether by way of indemnity, guarantee, or by reason of any breach of contract, or of statutory duty or by reason of tort (including but not limited to negligence) or any other legal principle or doctrine for any loss of profits, loss of use, loss of revenue, loss of data or loss of anticipated savings or for any financial or economic loss (whether direct or indirect) or for any consequential or indirect loss or damage whatsoever.

Reason:
Comment 65: Supplier requests for the inclusion of a consequential loss exclusion. As currently drafted, the Agreement does not distinguish between direct losses and indirect or consequential business losses. The proposed amendment reflects a standard commercial risk allocation by excluding remote and consequential losses, such as lost profits, revenue and other economic losses, which are often disproportionate to the scope and value of the supply.
